description: Sea, river or reservoir. The body remembers how. It lasts somewhere between four seconds and an afternoon and does not need to last longer.

The savoring research is blunt about this: negative stimuli dominate attention, so noticing a good moment is a practised capacity rather than an automatic one. People who savour report more uplifts later - the attention appears to come first.
notes: Amplifying savoring prospectively predicted increased uplift frequency over three months; uplifts did not predict savoring.

aspect: Better with one other person, worse with six
description: This category is unusual: it is improved by exactly one companion who also does not need to talk, and degraded by a group.
Access to a specific place - a coast, a grove, a field, a sky without light in it. Which is where land, movement and permits quietly decide who gets this.
energy_note: Free once you are there, and getting there is the question.
notes: Pairs with land, movement and settler-access categories in assets/text/palestine and assets/text/nigeria.

description: Swimming in water you can stand up in stops being an event and becomes a reference point - retold, compared against, and eventually shorthand inside one family for a whole kind of day.
energy_note: It turns into the story about it.
notes: Experiential purchases retain value through memory where material ones decay; people are markedly unwilling to trade the memory away.
